name: Motor-imagery decoders, offline benchmark against online use

provenance.how: Values transcribed by hand from Tables 2 and 3 of the paper named in `source`, retrieved 2026-09-12, and cross-checked by re-reading four rows and the two threshold claims independently before recording.
provenance.not_ours: Nothing here is computed by this project. These are the authors' reported figures; where a cell is absent it is because the paper does not report it, and it is omitted rather than filled.
provenance.scope: Four healthy participants, aged 20-28, four-class motor imagery, 2 s windows at 256 Hz. A small study. The point of shipping it is the offline/online contrast, not the leaderboard.

notes: Accuracy in percent, mean over participants, with the paper's reported standard deviation alongside.
The two methods are evaluation protocols, not models: `offline` replays recorded data, `online` is live closed-loop BCI operation with the same decoder.
Ten decoders were run under both protocols; ten more were run offline only, and those carry no `online` row rather than an imputed one.
No value is converted, rescaled or averaged across protocols. A claim that does not name a protocol does not resolve.
Four participants. Treat every number here as an illustration of protocol sensitivity rather than as a ranking of decoders.
